reconcile.connective: Commentators read the "unknown name" as a distinct, incommunicable divine name — not a denial of Jesus's other known titles.

discrepancy.connective: Skeptic's Annotated Bible compiler Steve Wells presses the objection directly, juxtaposing 19:12's unknown name against the Bible's own catalogue of Jesus's titles.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: Skeptic's Annotated Bible — "What was Jesus H. Christ's real name?"
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "What was Jesus H. Christ's real name?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com)

excerpts.excerpt_text: And he had a name written that no man knew but he himself; which seems to be his name, the Son of God … or else his name Immanuel.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Interprets the 'unknown name' of 19:12 as the Son of God/Immanuel — a name distinct from the titles (Word of God, King of Kings) the same chapter says are written and known, resolving the apparent clash.

excerpts.excerpt_text: A name written, that no man knew - This is a reference to what the rabbins call the shem hammephorash, or tetragrammaton, יהוה Yhvh; or what we call Jehovah. … This, therefore, is the name which no man knew but he himself.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Identifies the 'unknown name' specifically as the Tetragrammaton, a name Jews themselves never pronounce — a distinct name from Jesus's other titles, not a claim he has no known name at all.

excerpts.excerpt_text: name . . . called--His essential characteristics shall be.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: States plainly that the OT 'names' given to the Messiah (Wonderful, Counsellor, etc.) denote characteristics, not a literal proper name — addressing the 'category error' point that titles aren't legal names.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible, comm. on Revelation 19:12 (1746-63)
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats Revelation 19:12's 'unknown name' directly, identifying it with the Son of God/Immanuel and distinguishing it from the titles (Word of God, King of kings) the same chapter says are written and known — the harmonizing tradition's standard move on this exact verse.
